ops.text: Four independent causes, none an infra flake: (1) lint: the port's new gosec taint/IV/sha1 sites and two errorlint comparisons, later four more mechanical findings (unused darwin-only helper, G101 on synthetic secrets, gofumpt, prealloc); (2) release-assets: verify-release-archives.sh asserted macOS `file` wording for Mach-O binaries, which GNU libmagic orders differently, and the failure was silent under set -e; (3) test-linux/linux-smoke Go step: untagged tests written against the Darwin registry and store shape (arc as a second local browser, no meta table, XDG_CONFIG_HOME not isolated so fixtures collided in the runner's real config dir, an 8-minute hang on `<-consent.entered` once arc lookup failed), plus chrome_crashpad setsid()ing out of the daemonkit session in the real-Chrome smoke, `cookiesync uninstall` resolving a never-placed program inside daemonkit v0.32.1 inventoryClear, and one test expecting every Chrome profile to auto-register when the product registers one primary profile per browser; (4) the scripts/linux-smoke.sh step itself never failed.

Four independent causes, none an infra flake: (1) lint: the port's new gosec taint/IV/sha1 sites and two errorlint comparisons, later four more mechanical findings (unused darwin-only helper, G101 on synthetic secrets, gofumpt, prealloc); (2) release-assets: verify-release-archives.sh asserted macOS `file` wording for Mach-O binaries, which GNU libmagic orders differently, and the failure was silent under set -e; (3) test-linux/linux-smoke Go step: untagged tests written against the Darwin registry and store shape (arc as a second local browser, no meta table, XDG_CONFIG_HOME not isolated so fixtures collided in the runner's real config dir, an 8-minute hang on `<-consent.entered` once arc lookup failed), plus chrome_crashpad setsid()ing out of the daemonkit session in the real-Chrome smoke, `cookiesync uninstall` resolving a never-placed program inside daemonkit v0.32.1 inventoryClear, and one test expecting every Chrome profile to auto-register when the product registers one primary profile per browser; (4) the scripts/linux-smoke.sh step itself never failed.
